quotes.text: AI is not transformation, it is amplification. If the structure underneath your work is strong, AI compresses your effort and speeds up synthesis by reducing the manual drag people have carried for years.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that AI amplifies existing structure rather than transforming it.

quotes.text: This is why I frame access cleanup as relevance engineering rather than a boring compliance exercise. The real business question is who should see what to make better decisions with the least amount of drag.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes permission cleanup from a security chore into a lever for answer quality.

quotes.text: The metric that truly matters is decision latency which measures how long it takes for a person or a team to move from a question to a confident action.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete alternative to activity metrics for judging AI value.

quotes.text: Labels, ownership and version control are not just boring admin tasks. They are declarations of intent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why classification is a business declaration of importance, not compliance decoration.

quotes.text: If nobody clearly owns the source material, then nobody can truly own the answer the machine provides.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why unclear ownership turns into an AI failure pattern.

takeaways: AI in Microsoft 365 does not fix unclear ownership, messy access or duplicated content; it exposes them at machine speed.
Least privilege becomes relevance engineering in the AI era, because broad permissions turn stale and out-of-scope content into decision context.
Measure AI success by decision latency without loss of trust, and only reintroduce Copilot where access, ownership and decision flows are aligned.
hook: Your Copilot rollout looked ready, yet answers feel generic, people double-check everything and adoption stalls after a few weeks. This episode is for leaders and Microsoft 365 owners who want to understand why AI exposes broken permissions, weak classification and unclear ownership instead of fixing them. You get a five-step sequence to clean up the environment before scaling AI.
